segments.text: State succession asks what happens to international rights and obligations when responsibility for a territory changes from one state to another.
Prepare succession in relation to treaties, property, debts, archives and nationality. The rules vary with the type of succession and the legal instrument involved.

State succession occurs when one state replaces another in responsibility for the international relations of a territory. The legal result depends on the kind of succession—such as transfer of territory, separation, dissolution or decolonization—and on the category of right or obligation involved.

There is no single rule that every treaty automatically continues or automatically ends. Treaty succession, state property, archives, debts and nationality raise different questions and may be governed by treaty, custom, agreement between successor states or specific institutional practice.

Boundary treaties and territorial regimes receive special protection because stability of borders is a fundamental interest of international order. A change of sovereignty does not normally permit a successor state to reopen an established boundary simply by rejecting the predecessor's treaty.

For other treaties, continuity may depend on the type of succession and treaty. Newly independent states historically generated the 'clean slate' debate, while dissolution and separation often involve questions of continuity, succession or negotiated allocation.

Always identify the event first. Did one state dissolve completely, did part of a state separate, or was territory transferred? Then identify the legal category—treaty, debt, property, archive or nationality. Only after these steps should the applicable rule be stated.

items.text: State succession occurs when responsibility for a territory shifts from one state to another. The legal consequences depend on the kind of succession and the type of right or obligation involved.
Study treaty succession, state property, archives, debts and nationality separately because international law does not apply one identical rule to all categories.
Dissolution, separation, transfer of territory and decolonization can create different legal questions. Always identify the factual type of succession before stating a rule.
Boundary arrangements are treated with special stability because international order depends on settled territorial limits.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not answer succession questions with a single formula that “all obligations transfer” or “no obligations transfer.” The result is category-specific.
